MECHANISM_RESOLVED_2026-08-03.corrects_a_garbled_prior_citation: FUNC_800502C4_fmv_sequence_completion_check.md's own prior static-inference pass garbled the array address as '0x800a-18312' (likely a naming-script formatting bug). Fully disassembled the function (asm/hand_written/800502c4_sub_800502c4.s, cross-verified instruction-for-instruction against the raw pristine listing asm/nonmatchings/resident/800502c4.s -- exact match, every instruction word identical): the 16-byte per-level completion array is at 0x8009B878, computed as 0x800A0000 - 0x4788 (18312 decimal), NOT '0x800a-18312' as a literal address.
MECHANISM_RESOLVED_2026-08-03.structure: One byte per level (16 total, indices 0-15). A level's own value transitions from 0 to exactly 7 (0b111) when that level reaches 100% completion. 7 == 3 bits, plausibly one per completion axis (grain/FLIK/seed, matching the shared 3-counter results-screen convention already established for F06/F15 this session) -- the exact per-axis bit-set instructions were not independently traced this pass, this is inferred from the value and timing, not proven bit-by-bit.
MECHANISM_RESOLVED_2026-08-03.per_level_clip_trigger: When a level index v1 (read from a halfword at 0x8008245C, inferred to mean 'the level that just finished') has array[v1]==7 for the FIRST time (guarded against re-firing by a check against gp+1268/0x80082290), that level's own FMV clip plays: FMV id read from a 16-entry table at 0x80077FE3+v1, passed to the play-FMV call 0x8003e7c0(fmv_id, -1).
MECHANISM_RESOLVED_2026-08-03.campaign_wide_ending_trigger: Separately, and always: sums all 16 array bytes. If the sum==112 (all 16 levels at value 7 -- full 100% campaign completion), plays FMV id 41 (already live-confirmed this session as the game's true ending cutscene, via D20/F15's own investigation) and sets bit 0x02 in the adjacent byte 0x8009B888.
MECHANISM_RESOLVED_2026-08-03.distinct_from_bonus_challenge_system: SYS_bonus_unlock_challenges.md's own 0x8009B889 byte (3 packed low bits for the hidden spider/mushroom/grasshopper challenges) is a SEPARATE, smaller mechanism -- not the same as this 16-byte per-level array, despite being immediately adjacent in memory.

MENU_READER_FOUND_2026-08-03.menu_availability_builder: Exactly ONE reader of the unlock array fired across the whole movie: PC 0x800b4120, inside a frontend-overlay function with prologue at 0x800b4084 (addiu sp,sp,-192; functionBounds reports a merged overlay region, typical). One single pass at emulator frame 8718 (~4s after the anchor), reading array indices 1-15 -- index 0 is never checked, consistent with slot 0 (the intro clip) being availability-gated by campaign progress instead. Disassembly of 0x800b40e0..0x800b4188 decodes the COMPLETE availability model, four gate classes into a per-slot menu-state buffer on the stack: (1) STORY clips: a loop marks slots available up to the campaign-progress halfword 0x80082284 (the same halfword FUNC_80055478 serializes at buffer+1); (2) BONUS clips: for s0=1..15, array[s0]==7 (100% completion) marks the paired slot; (3) 0x8009B888 bits 0x01/0x02 gate two more entries (bit 0x02 = the campaign-100% ending flag set by FUNC_800502C4); (4) 0x8009B889 (the separate 3-bit hidden-challenge byte) gates the bonus-challenge clips. This single function ties together every unlock source previously documented separately.
